&reftitle.returnvalues;
Returns the key on success&return.falseforfailure;.
The key is returned as a raw string. When working with inifile databases this string has the form "[group]value_name", or simply "value_name" when there is no group; dba_key_split converts it back into a [group, value_name] array.
On inifile databases, iterating over a non-empty group also returns the group header itself (for example "[group]") as a key in its own right, in addition to the keys it contains. dba_key_split turns such a key into [group, ""], with an empty value name.
On inifile databases, writing to the database (with dba_insert, dba_replace or dba_delete) between calls to dba_firstkey and dba_nextkey silently ends the iteration, even when the write does not affect the current key or group: the next call returns &false;, although the data itself is not affected. The restitution order also follows the physical order of the underlying file, not the logical insertion order: replacing or re-inserting an existing key moves it to the end of the iteration.
On a cdb database opened for writing (handler cdb_make), dba_nextkey always returns &false;, since such a database cannot be read until it has been closed and reopened for reading.
